Retain the already successful SECOND CHARACTER peeking naturally from behind the adult/sofa, with hands holding the shoulder/backrest and body occluded. Do not move it to the foreground.
2) Keep exactly ONE existing white A4 sheet at the SAME POSITION, size and perspective, and exactly ONE small smartphone at its SAME position near the family. The SHEET remains COMPLETELY BLANK for a later exact original cropped worksheet insert; NO generated writing, maze, icons, decoder, letters, QR or maps. The PHONE screen remains BLANK very dark near-black, all FOUR INNER SCREEN CORNERS clearly visible, not covered by fingers or characters. Keep the phone lying naturally on wood, realistic bezel thickness, rounded inner screen corners, subtle non-uniform real glass reflections, contact shadow. Light the sheet naturally in this same room: subtle ivory paper fibres, warm practical light from right and cool light from left, gentle local brightness/shadows, a very slight physical edge lift of 1–2mm at a corner and thin real edge shadow, not a warped or floating sheet. Preserve its flat useful print plane. Objects must feel photographed in the room.
3) Add one or two ordinary DARK BLUE/BLACK ballpoint pens and ONE coloured felt-tip marker as specified below. Retain the existing wooden pencil. The COLOURED marker lies DIAGONALLY partly OVER a corner of the BLANK PAPER, crossing from wood onto paper with a real soft contact shadow crossing onto the paper. It obscures only a small corner, not the main clue area. Pens naturally rest at slightly different angles on wood, one may partly cross another paper edge. Matte solid coloured pen/marker bodies with no white barrels, no metallic reflections, NO branding/text. Realistic everyday school stationery, not oversized. Everything has consistent perspective, believable contact and cast shadows. Do not draw lines on the paper.
4) Add exactly ONE ADDITIONAL tiny character matching Image 2, hidden tastefully in the background in the position specified below. Only about 4–6% image height, smaller and less contrasty than the existing shoulder-peeking character. Match the ambient shadow/amber light, partly hide it behind a book/leaf/frame. It should be an enjoyable SECOND-LOOK easter egg, difficult to notice at first glance, not glowing, not brightly outlined, not pasted in front. Keep original soft painted pixel style and silhouette, no generic redesign, no text/name.
No extra props, people, papers, phones or characters beyond these. No words, typography, logo, watermark, button, graphic trails. Preserve all successful original composition, original room and human realism.
